meta.title: Which AWS certification fits you?
meta.subtitle: Answer a few questions about your studies and goals, and get a recommended first certification and a next step.
meta.disclaimer: Exam versions, prices and dates change. Always check the official AWS page before booking.
meta.price_note: Prices are AWS list prices in USD before tax; local prices may differ.

r_clf_business.reason: You'll learn the language of the cloud: what the main AWS services do, how pricing works and how security responsibilities are shared. No coding needed, which makes it ideal if you work alongside tech teams.

r_aif_business.reason: It explains AI, machine learning and generative AI in plain terms, with real use cases. Once you know how the technology works, AI Business Strategist adds the strategy and governance side.

r_aib.reason: This one is built for people who decide about AI rather than build it: choosing investments, building the business case and scaling adoption responsibly. AI Practitioner is a good companion if you also want the technical basics.

r_clf_tech.reason: A quick, low-pressure way to get the big picture of AWS. With a tech background you can move on to Solutions Architect – Associate soon after.

r_aif_tech.reason: It gives you the AI, ML and generative AI vocabulary and the AWS services behind it. Machine Learning Engineer – Associate is the natural hands-on next step.

r_saa.reason: The most popular technical AWS certification. You'll learn to combine compute, storage, networking and databases into systems that are secure, resilient and cost-efficient.

r_dva.reason: Made for people who write code that runs on AWS: serverless functions, APIs, databases and deployment pipelines. DevOps Engineer – Professional is where this path leads.

r_cloudops.reason: Focused on running workloads well: monitoring, troubleshooting, automation and reliability. It used to be called SysOps Administrator, and it leads naturally to DevOps Engineer – Professional.

r_dea.reason: You'll learn to build data pipelines and data stores on AWS. Good data foundations are what AI and ML run on, so ML Engineer – Associate is a strong next step.

r_security_start.reason: Security – Specialty expects real experience, so start with Solutions Architect – Associate. It builds the base that cloud security sits on: identity and access, networking and encryption.

r_mla.reason: It covers the full ML workflow on AWS: preparing data, training, deploying and maintaining models. Generative AI Developer – Professional is the advanced step if you move toward LLM products.

r_genai_start.reason: Generative AI Developer – Professional is the cert for building LLM apps, but it is a professional-level exam. AI Practitioner is a quick first win that covers generative AI concepts and the AWS services behind them. If you already build on AWS every day, you can aim for the professional exam directly.

r_aif_explore.reason: The best way to get the big picture of AI, ML and generative AI before choosing a direction. Afterwards, ML Engineer – Associate takes you hands-on.

r_sap.reason: Built for designing complex AWS solutions across many accounts, including migrations and hybrid setups. It's one of the most respected AWS certifications.

r_dop.reason: Validates CI/CD, infrastructure as code, monitoring and automation for distributed systems at scale. Security – Specialty pairs well with it.

r_aip.reason: The newest professional certification, built for engineers shipping generative AI products on AWS with services like Amazon Bedrock.

r_ml_next.reason: The Machine Learning – Specialty exam was retired in March 2026, so ML Engineer – Associate is now AWS's main ML certification. Generative AI Developer – Professional is the advanced step after it.

r_scs.reason: The dedicated AWS security certification: identity and access, data protection, detection and incident response.

r_networking.reason: The Advanced Networking – Specialty exam is being retired at the end of 2026. Solutions Architect – Professional is the strongest current option and covers network connectivity design for large and hybrid setups.

r_research_compute_clf.reason: With a few weeks, Cloud Practitioner is a realistic first step. You'll learn how renting computing power works, what it costs and how to keep data safe. Solutions Architect – Associate then teaches you to design the setups that big simulations need.

r_research_compute_saa.reason: Solutions Architect – Associate teaches you to choose and combine compute, storage and networking on AWS, which is what large simulations and calculations need. If your results feed into machine learning, ML Engineer – Associate is a good next step.

r_research_data_clf.reason: With a few weeks, Cloud Practitioner is a realistic first step: you'll understand how cloud storage and computing work and what they cost. Data Engineer – Associate is the hands-on certificate for building pipelines around large research datasets.

r_research_data_dea.reason: Data Engineer – Associate teaches you to build pipelines and data stores for datasets far too big for a laptop. Once your data is in good shape, ML Engineer – Associate shows you how to train models on it.

r_research_ml_aif.reason: With a few weeks, AI Practitioner gives you a solid grounding in machine learning, generative AI and the AWS services behind them. ML Engineer – Associate is the hands-on step for training and deploying your own models.

r_research_ml_mla.reason: ML Engineer – Associate covers the workflow your research would use: preparing data, training, deploying and monitoring models on AWS. Generative AI Developer – Professional is the advanced step if you move toward LLM-based tools.

r_sci_clf.reason: Cloud Practitioner gives you the big picture: what the cloud is, how universities and companies use it, what it costs and how security works. No coding needed. AI Practitioner is a natural follow-up.

r_sci_aif.reason: AI Practitioner explains AI, machine learning and generative AI in plain terms, with real use cases. It needs no coding, so it fits well if you want to follow how AI is changing research. Cloud Practitioner adds the cloud basics.

r_sci_build.reason: Cloud Practitioner is a gentle start that needs no coding. While you learn Python or SQL, aim for Data Engineer – Associate next: it's about building pipelines for large datasets, a skill research groups and companies both need.

r_sci_career_dea.reason: Data Engineer – Associate shows you can build the pipelines and data stores that analytics and AI depend on, and your science background is a real advantage there. ML Engineer – Associate is the next step.

r_sci_career_mla.reason: ML Engineer – Associate shows you can take machine learning from experiments to production on AWS. Combined with your scientific field, that makes a strong profile. Generative AI Developer – Professional is the advanced step.

r_sci_career_saa.reason: Solutions Architect – Associate is the most popular technical AWS certification and a common first credential for cloud jobs. Developer – Associate adds the coding side.

r_sci_career_mgmt.reason: Cloud Practitioner helps you talk confidently with engineers and understand cloud costs and risks. AI Business Strategist then adds AI strategy and governance, which is useful in management, consulting and policy roles.

r_biz_aib.reason: Your role is to decide about AI, or advise others on it, rather than build it. This certification tests exactly that judgment: which projects are worth it, the business case and governance. No coding needed. AI Practitioner adds the technical basics.

r_biz_lead_clf.reason: Cloud Practitioner helps you understand what your tech teams and suppliers are talking about, how cloud pricing works and where the risks are. AI Business Strategist adds AI strategy on top.

r_biz_consult_clf.reason: Cloud Practitioner covers the business side of the cloud: pricing models, cost control, security and the main services. That's what clients ask about when they move to the cloud. AI Business Strategist prepares you for AI projects.

r_biz_consult_aif.reason: AI Practitioner teaches what AI and generative AI can and can't do, so you can recommend realistic use cases to clients. AI Business Strategist then covers business cases and governance.

r_biz_product_clf.reason: Product and project managers in tech work with engineers every day. Cloud Practitioner gives you the shared language: services, costs, security and reliability. AI Practitioner is a strong addition.

r_biz_product_aif.reason: To manage an AI product, you need to know what models can do, what they cost and where they fail. AI Practitioner covers that without coding. AI Business Strategist adds strategy and governance.

r_biz_sales_clf.reason: Cloud Practitioner helps you explain cloud services, pricing and security to customers with confidence. AI Practitioner is a natural next step as more products include AI.

r_biz_sales_aif.reason: AI Practitioner helps you understand the AI solutions you sell and answer customers' questions accurately. AI Business Strategist adds the business case and governance side.

r_biz_founder_clf.reason: Cloud Practitioner teaches the AWS basics a founder needs: the main services, pricing and how to avoid surprise bills. If you end up building the product yourself, Solutions Architect – Associate is the next step.

r_biz_founder_aif.reason: AI Practitioner shows you what AI and generative AI can realistically do for a product and which AWS services exist for it. AI Business Strategist helps you build the business case.

r_biz_ai_aif.reason: With your data skills, AI Practitioner helps you spot where AI and generative AI can improve business processes, and which AWS services exist for it. AI Business Strategist adds the business case and governance.

r_biz_switch.reason: Cloud Practitioner is a quick first credential that shows you understand the cloud. Your SQL and Python are a good base for Data Engineer – Associate, the AWS certification closest to data roles.

r_biz_data_clf.reason: With a few weeks, Cloud Practitioner is a realistic first step: you'll learn where company data lives in the cloud and what it costs. Data Engineer – Associate is the hands-on step for building analytics pipelines.

r_biz_data_dea.reason: Data Engineer – Associate teaches you to build the pipelines and data stores that dashboards and reports depend on. ML Engineer – Associate is the step after if you want to move into predictive analytics.

r_soc_clf.reason: Cloud Practitioner explains what happens behind the apps and websites you use every day: where data is stored, how services scale and how security works. No coding needed. AI Practitioner is a good next step.

r_soc_aib.reason: AI Business Strategist focuses on decisions, governance and responsible AI, not on coding or AWS services. It suits people who want to shape how organizations use AI. AI Practitioner adds the technical basics.

r_soc_aif.reason: AI Practitioner explains how AI, machine learning and generative AI work, what they're good at and where they fail. That helps you use AI tools well and judge their output. AI Business Strategist is a good follow-up.

r_soc_aif_research.reason: To study AI's impact on people, it helps to know how the technology actually works. AI Practitioner covers that without coding, including responsible AI. AI Business Strategist adds the organizational and governance side.

r_soc_career.reason: Cloud Practitioner is a quick first step that shows employers you understand the cloud. Data Engineer – Associate is the AWS certification closest to data work. It's more technical, so build up your Python or SQL alongside it.

clf.name: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner
clf.summary: Shows you understand the AWS Cloud as a whole: core services, pricing and billing, security basics and global infrastructure. Not tied to any job role.

aif.name: AWS Certified AI Practitioner
aif.summary: Covers the foundations of AI, machine learning and generative AI, their use cases, and the AWS services that support them.
aif.good_for: Anyone who wants to understand AI on AWS before going deeper.

aib.name: AWS Certified AI Business Strategist
aib.summary: Tests business judgment for AI: which AI investments to pursue, how to build the business case, governance and responsible AI, and scaling adoption. No coding, and it does not test AWS services.
aib.note: Currently offered as a beta exam.

saa.name: AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate
saa.summary: Designing secure, resilient, high-performing and cost-efficient systems on AWS, based on the AWS Well-Architected Framework.
saa.good_for: The classic first technical cert; AWS recommends it for people moving into cloud careers.

dva.name: AWS Certified Developer – Associate
dva.summary: Developing, deploying and debugging cloud-based applications on AWS.
dva.good_for: Developers who write code that runs on AWS.
dva.note: A new exam version that adds AI-assisted development tools starts on 1 Dec 2026; the current version can be taken until 30 Nov 2026.

cloudops.name: AWS Certified CloudOps Engineer – Associate
cloudops.summary: Deploying, managing and operating workloads on AWS: monitoring, troubleshooting, automation, security controls and networking. Formerly called SysOps Administrator – Associate.
cloudops.good_for: People who like keeping systems healthy and running.

dea.name: AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate
dea.summary: Building data pipelines and data stores on AWS and optimizing their cost and performance.
dea.good_for: Data-minded students heading toward data or AI engineering.

mla.name: AWS Certified Machine Learning Engineer – Associate
mla.summary: Implementing, deploying and maintaining AI and ML solutions on AWS.
mla.good_for: People who want to build and run ML models, not just use them.
mla.note: The exam was updated to a new version in 2026; use the latest exam guide when studying.

sap.name: AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional
sap.summary: Designing complex, optimized AWS solutions based on the Well-Architected Framework. Intended for people with 2+ years of hands-on experience.
sap.good_for: Experienced architects working across many accounts and services.
sap.note: The exam is being updated: the current version can be taken until 16 Nov 2026, then the new version replaces it.

dop.name: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer – Professional
dop.summary: Provisioning, operating and managing distributed application systems on AWS, including CI/CD, automation and infrastructure as code. Intended for people with 2+ years of experience.
dop.good_for: Developers and operations engineers who automate everything.

aip.name: AWS Certified Generative AI Developer – Professional
aip.summary: Designing, building and deploying production generative AI solutions on AWS, using services like Amazon Bedrock.
aip.note: AWS suggests AI Practitioner, Solutions Architect – Associate, ML Engineer – Associate and/or Data Engineer – Associate as helpful preparation.

scs.name: AWS Certified Security – Specialty
scs.summary: Securing AWS workloads and applications: identity and access, data protection, detection and incident response.
